title: Incident stakeholder mapping, escalation matrix, and customer comm templates
author: Leah Kim
content:
Overview

This page defines the stakeholder mapping, escalation matrix, and reusable customer / status-page communication templates we use for operational incidents that impact Redwood Inference services. It consolidates ownership, timing, and message templates so on-call responders can quickly bring the right people into an incident and maintain consistent, professional customer communication.

Scope

- Applies to all production incidents for Redwood-hosted inference endpoints, Dedicated control-plane issues, and Private control plane incidents where Redwood is the escalation contact.
- Does NOT replace service-specific runbooks; it standardizes who to notify and how to communicate.

Incident severities (standardized)

Table: Severity definitions and thresholds (engineers: use metrics from service-slo-matrix page)

1) Sev 1 (P1) – System down or large-scale data loss
   - Impact: >30% of traffic or critical control-plane outage preventing inference across regions.
   - Target response: 0–5 min pager acknowledge, IC assigned within 10 min.
   - Escalation: Immediate to oncall, SRE lead, Eng manager, and CSE/Support.

2) Sev 2 (P2) – Major functionality degraded
   - Impact: 5–30% of traffic or sustained latency SLO miss > 2 min.
   - Target response: 5–15 min acknowledge, IC assigned within 30 min.

3) Sev 3 (P3) – Partial/isolated impact
   - Impact: <5% of traffic, minor errors for single customer or model variant.
   - Target response: 1 business hour acknowledge, remediation planned within 24 hours.

4) Sev 4 (P4) – Informational or scheduled maintenance
   - Impact: No immediate customer disruption; changes tracked via release notes.

Roles and ownership

- Incident Commander (IC): owns operational decisions and runbook execution until handover. Typical senior SRE/Platform engineer.
- Communications Lead (Comms): drafts status updates, liaises with Customer Success (CS), Legal, and Sales for customer-facing messaging.
- Subject Matter Experts (SME): model-serving runtime, infra, networking, or customer integration engineers called as needed.
- Customer Success Liaison (CS Liaison): responsible for targeted customer notifications and post-incident follow-up.
- Exec Liaison: notifies leadership for P1s and cross-org impacts.
- Postmortem Author: owns the writeup and action-item tracking after LT recovery.

Stakeholder mapping (quick reference)

- Runtime CPU/GPU anomalies -> SME: Runtime team (runtime@redwood.example.com)
- High token cost / cost-regression observed -> SME: Optimize team
- Latency SLO miss affecting multiple customers -> SME: SRE + Runtime, IC assigns leads
- Customer-visible errors (single customer) -> CS Liaison + Integration Engineer
- Security incident (data exfiltration, credential compromise) -> Security oncall + Legal + IC

Escalation matrix and timings (procedural)

1) Page / Acknowledge
   - Pager hits primary oncall -> 1st responder acknowledges in pager within defined response window.
   - If no ack, 2nd-level escalation after 5 minutes (P1) or 15 minutes (P2). Automation must escalate via PagerDuty escalation policy.

2) Assign IC and Comms (within 10 min for P1, 30 min for P2)
   - IC declares incident severity and documents scope in incident channel header.

3) Gather initial triage (first 20 minutes for P1)
   - IC collects: telemetry snapshot, affected regions, % traffic impacted, recent deploys, changelogs.
   - Attach runbook pointers (list below).

4) Mobilize SMEs (30–60 minutes)
   - IC pages specific SMEs. Clearly state: "Need: TPU/VM host metric, model KV cache checks, and recent kernel builds".

5) Customer comms cadence
   - Status posted to status.redwood.ai within 15 minutes of P1 detection. Subsequent updates every 30–60 minutes with new facts until recovery.

6) Recovery and verification
   - IC confirms recovery via SLO metrics and customer success checks. Declare "Service recovered" on status page and close incident when verification passes for two consecutive 5-minute windows.

7) Post-incident activities
   - Postmortem draft due in 72 hours for P1, 5 business days for P2. Action items assigned with owners and due dates.

Runbook pointers (reference commands and checks)

- Telemetry snapshot: (Grafana + Loki + Jaeger)
  - grafana: /d/service-overview – set time window: -15m to now.
  - loki query: {service="runtime"} |= "error" | count_over_time(15m)
- Quick health checks (CLI examples)
  - curl -sS https://health-api.redwood.internal/v1/services/runtime/health | jq
  - kubectl get pods -n runtime -o wide --selector=component=inference
  - rlog tail runtime --since=10m --filter="error OR warn"
- Hotfix deploy template (if rollback required)
  - git checkout -b incident-hotfix && make build-image && deployctl promote --service runtime --image registry/release:hotfix-<sha>

Communication templates (copy-paste friendly)

1) Status page short form (P1 initial)
   - Title: Partial/Complete service outage affecting inference endpoints
   - Impact: Customers may experience increased latency or failed requests across multiple regions.
   - Current status: Investigating.
   - Next update: in 30 minutes or sooner as new information becomes available.
   - Note: We are treating this as Sev 1 and have SRE and runtime teams actively investigating.

2) Status page recovery update (P1)
   - Title: Service recovered — monitoring ongoing
   - Impact: The service is responding normally. We are monitoring to ensure stable metrics.
   - Current status: Mitigated; full recovery confirmed at <timestamp UTC>.
   - Next update: Post-incident report and root-cause analysis planned within 72 hours.

3) Customer-facing email template (for affected customers)
   - Subject: Incident update — service disruption on <date> (Incident ID: <INC-XXXX>)
   - Body: Hello <CustomerName>,

     We detected a disruption to Redwood Inference on <date> which affected requests to <affected-endpoint>. Our on-call teams declared this a Sev 1 incident and worked to mitigate the issue. The service returned to normal at <recovery-timestamp UTC>.

     What happened: <short summary — two sentences>.
     Impact: <who/what was affected>.
     What we did: <actions taken>.
     Next steps: We will publish a post-incident report with root cause analysis and action items within 72 hours. Your dedicated CS contact <CS-name> will follow up directly if you were specifically affected.

     If you have immediate concerns, reply to this email or contact <CS-phone-or-slack>.

     Sincerely,
     Redwood Inference Operations Team

4) Slack incident channel pinned update (concise)
   - [HH:MM UTC] INVESTIGATING — Identified increase in 500s for /v1/generate; paging runtime oncall. Traffic impacted ~18%.
   - [HH:MM UTC] MITIGATED — Rolling restart of inference pool completed; monitoring for stabilization.

5) CS handoff template (internal)
   - Incident ID: <INC-XXXX>
   - Summary: <one-line summary>
   - Affected customers: <list>
   - Known risk: <details>
   - Recommended customer messaging: <link to status page or copy>

Postmortem outline (required fields)

- Title and incident ID
- Summary (1–3 sentences)
- Severity and duration (start, mitigation, recovery)
- Impact (customers, SLOs)
- Timeline of events (minute-granular for P1)
- Root cause analysis (technical and process causes)
- Action items (owner + due date + verification criteria)
- Lessons learned and follow-ups (game-day, training, automation needs)

On-call rotation fairness, shadowing, and game-day plan

- Rotation policy: Primary oncall rotates weekly; secondary/backup rotates monthly. Swap requests handled via oncall-swap@redwood.example.com and must include a proposed replacement and overlap window.
- Shadowing: New oncall engineers must shadow for two full rotation cycles before primary handoff; shadow shift checklist available in team wiki.
- Compensation: Oncall pay and PTO credit per company policy (see people-ops handbook page 02_roles-and-career).
- Game-day schedule: Quarterly cross-team exercises; each exercise has a pre-defined incident scenario, a runbook validation step, and a 2-hour forced recovery window. Post-game-day retro required within 3 business days.

Measurement and metrics (what to track)

- Pager response time (median and 95th)
- Time-to-IC assignment for P1s
- Time-to-first-customer-status-post
- Mean time to mitigation (MTTM) and mean time to recovery (MTTR) by severity
- Postmortem completion rate and action item closure rate

Appendix: Quick contact matrix (use PagerDuty/Okta to get live contact info)

- Oncall SRE: @sre-oncall (PagerDuty)
- Runtime oncall: @runtime-oncall (PagerDuty)
- CS Liaison: cs-ops@redwood.example.com
- Security oncall: sec-oncall@redwood.example.com

Flow example (ASCII)

Pager -> Acknowledge -> IC assigned -> Channel created (#inc-INC-XXXX) -> Post status -> Mobilize SMEs -> Mitigate -> Verify -> Recover -> Postmortem

Owner and maintenance

- Document owner: Leah Kim (engineering) — responsible for annual review and updates after every P1.
- Review cadence: Semi-annual review, and edit after any major tooling or process change.
